results.title: SSH is not reachable from the internet on a private ingress host
results.subject: port:tcp/22
results.message: SSH answers from outside on port 22 at 192.0.2.30 (SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.2p1 Debian-2+deb12u3); profile unknown, judged as if nothing should be public; pass --profile to judge against your ingress

fix.hint: Make SSH work over the tailnet first, then close the public SSH rule in the host firewall and the provider firewall (see SSH and NET checks).

results.title: Web ports do not answer on the raw IP behind a tunnel
results.subject: port:tcp/443
results.message: port 443 (HTTPS) could not be checked on 2001:db8:2::30 (network is unreachable); closed or filtered on 192.0.2.30

fix.hint: Publish the proxy on 127.0.0.1 only and let the tunnel connector reach it locally, then drop the public 80 and 443 rules in the provider firewall.

results.title: Docker API ports are not reachable from the internet
results.subject: port:tcp/2375
results.message: port 2375 (Docker API) could not be checked on 2001:db8:2::30 (network is unreachable); closed or filtered on 192.0.2.30

fix.hint: Remove the tcp:// listener from the Docker daemon (hosts in daemon.json, -H in the service unit) and reach Docker over SSH or the tailnet instead.

results.title: The app hostname answers over HTTPS without TLS or redirect anomalies
results.subject: host
results.message: no --hostname given; pass --hostname app.example.com to check it over HTTPS

fix.hint: Behind a tunnel, turn off the app's own redirect to HTTPS (or trust the proxy's X-Forwarded-Proto) and let the tunnel enforce HTTPS; renew or fix the certificate when verification fails.
